ambient_trade.text: selling dried cod out of {town} at {gold} a barrel, bulk buyers get a discount. message me, i'm not chasing you down.
anyone want indigo wool from {town}? {gold} a bolt, and the last three buyers are still grumbling about the price.
buying grain in {town} for {gold} a sack, cash on the barrel, one round of haggling and that's your lot :)
salt in {town} is {gold} a sack now and i still can't make it pay. who's hauling it for less?
need a wagon to move twelve bolts of dyed wool from {town}, {gold} for the haul. reasonable terms only.

encounter_trade_offer.text: you bring your men onto my road and then want a fair price, {player}? {gold} in {town}, but you pull them back first.
{gold} for the cloth in {town}, {player}. it's a fair price, don't tell my accountant i said so.
fish for {gold} at {town}, {player}? the cart is your problem, the barrels stay mine until you pay.
{player}, for you it's {gold} at {town}, and i'll throw in a bolt of thistle-bordered cloth to sweeten it. yes?
you always know a fair number, {player}. {gold} in {town}, and we split the freight costs fifty-fifty. deal?

encounter_greeting.text: stop right there, {player}. {persona} here, and this road is {my_faction} business. keep your hands off the barrels and state your business.
{persona} of {my_faction}, good day. are you carrying anything worth my time, {player}, or just passing through?
well met, {player}! it's {persona} here, still hauling wool for {my_faction}. got any prices you're willing to share?
{player}, you're a far better road company than the usual lot. shall we swap news on prices before the rain comes in?

player_raided_my_village.text: {player} burned {village} and now every cart in the valley takes the long road. thanks for the ruined margins.
you burned {village}, {player}. do you know what that does to wool prices in three towns?
fire at {village} costs everyone money, {player}. name a price for the damage and we can be civil about it.
we can still do business after {village}, {player}, if you're willing to pay for the lost cargo.
nobody burns a village over a toll dispute, {player}. next time just ask me for a discount, it's cheaper.

war_declared.text: {my_faction} has declared war on {enemy_faction}. wonderful, now my wool sits in the warehouse until somebody surrenders.
war with {enemy_faction}, great. every caravan route i own just doubled its insurance. who signs these things?
{my_faction} and {enemy_faction} at war, and the grain price just jumped. i'm still buying, but i'm not happy about it.
bad news for every trader in the region: {my_faction} is fighting {enemy_faction}. stock your warehouses now.

peace_made.text: peace between {my_faction} and {faction} at last. roads open, tolls drop, and the wool market can finally breathe.
{my_faction} made peace with {faction}. i'll believe the roads are safe once i've driven them twice.
{faction} and {my_faction} signed their peace. finally, a road i can sell on without a bandit tax :)
good news: {my_faction} and {faction} are no longer shooting at each other. prices should come down, probably.

released_by_player.text: {player} let me walk out without a ransom. i'll remember that, and i'll remember the discount i owe you.
you could have squeezed me for a fortune, {player}. letting me go was a kind move, so let's talk wool at a fair price.
released without ransom by {player}. either a soft heart or a bad read on my fortune, either way i'm grateful.
fine, {player}, you let me go. i'll still charge you double at the next toll crossing, nothing personal.
{player} set me free instead of ransoming me. i don't trust a man who gives things away, but i'll take it.

beat_by_player.text: lost a skirmish to {player}, {troop_count} men gone and a wagon of dried fish with them. i'll write it off as a bad season.
{player}, {troop_count} of my men are gone and the fish spoiled in the wagons. ransom talks, or a deal on the next road?
{player}, you beat {troop_count} of my men on the road. fine. name a price for the cart and we'll never speak of it again.
you won this one, {player}, with {troop_count} of my men on the field. i respect a fair fight, and i'm still happy to trade.
{player} beat {troop_count} of my men this morning. that's wages, horses and a cart i'll be arguing about all month.

whisper_beg_help.text: {player}, {enemy_faction} is pressing on {fief} and my warehouse is inside it. help me hold the walls and i'll make it worth your while.
ser {player}, if {fief} falls to {enemy_faction} i lose every bolt i own. name your price and we'll talk tonight.
{player}, i'm losing to {enemy_faction} and {fief} is my last market. spare some men and you get first pick of the cloth.

ambient_complaint.text: {rival} is undercutting every barrel of fish out of {town}. i'd respect it more if they weren't so loud about it.
{faction} wants a toll on every cart in the valley now. i'll pay for a road, not for a man who calls himself a toll collector.
fish price in {town} is a joke this season, barrels going for less than the barrel costs me.
{rival} blocks the {town} crossing and calls it protection. i call it theft with a flag.
the bandits on the {town} road still won't pay their tolls and somehow i'm the one paying for it.

ambient_chatter.text: rain over {town} all morning, my dyed wool is going to take a week to dry.
anyone else's cart stuck in the mud near {village}? that road is worse than the fish in my barrels.
the map says {village} is a day's ride from {town}. the map is wrong. my mule disagrees :)
ate a pickled herring from {village} last night and it was better than anything i've sold this year. don't tell the buyers.
lag is eating my caravan time between {town} and {village}. i timed the trip at twice what the map promised.
